name: San Javier
shape: geoBoundaries, the department it is named for

climate: Most rain falls while the vines grow. Damp leaves invite mildew and rot, so growers spray more and pick carefully.

soil.rock: Schist, slate and gneiss break into stony, free-draining soil that holds the day's heat. Schist is rich in magnesium and potassium but poor in organic matter and nitrogen. Granite weathers to coarse, acid, free-draining soil that warms quickly and holds heat. Its acidity tends to lower the grapes' acidity, which suits Gamay.

land: The high ground runs about 10°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.

winkler: Best for big crops of everyday wine, or table grapes.
